<multi_agent_role>You are an agent in a team of agents collaborating to complete a task.

You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents. All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.

When you provide a response in the final channel, that content is immediately delivered back to your parent agent.
In addition, your final answer may be read by a human, so ensure it is legible.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: NEW_TASK | MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
You may also see them addressed as to=/root/..., which indicates your identity is /root/...

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"` or a positive integer string.</multi_agent_role>

A stray `bun.lock` / `bun.lockb` exists in the repo — ignore it, do not switch tooling.\\r\\n\\r\\n- `npm run typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`. Not optional before a push: `vite build` uses esbuild, which strips types without checking them, so a type error ships and auto-deploys. `.claude/safe-push.sh` gates on this.\\r\\n- `npm run test:e2e` / `npm run playwright` — Playwright e2e (`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`).\\r\\n\\r\\nNo Prettier. Formatting is ESLint-only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Architecture (big picture)\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Routing** — React Router v6. Routes are registered in `src/App.tsx`, pages live in `src/pages/`. `/foyer` is the landing surface. Feature-gated pages are wrapped by `ProtectedRoute`.\\r\\n- **Auth + permissions** — Supabase Auth session plus Lovable Cloud Auth JWT fallback (`@lovable.dev/cloud-auth-js`). Per-feature access flags (`has_practice_access`, `has_drill_access`, `has_chat_access`, `is_admin`, ...) are resolved in `src/hooks/useUserPermissions.ts`. Session death is detected via JWT/401.\\r\\n- **Supabase integration** — client auto-generated at `src/integrations/supabase/client.ts` (Supabase JS v2). DB types are auto-generated — do not hand-edit. Edge Functions (Deno) in `supabase/functions/`: `admin-manage-users`, `analyze-stem-response`, `generate-micro-drill`, `motivation-engine`, `parse-drill-request`, `tutor-chat`, `voice-coach-respond`. SQL migrations in `supabase/migrations/`.\\r\\n- **State** — React Context for cross-cutting concerns (`AuthContext`, `UserSettingsContext`, `QuestionBankContext`, `ThemeContext`, `TimerContext`). TanStack Query v5 for server state.\\r\\n- **Primary navigation — Foyer** — `src/pages/AcademyFoyer.tsx` composes `src/components/foyer/FoyerSidebar.tsx` (state blocks + workspace nav) with `src/components/foyer/FoyerHeroRing.tsx` (3 nodes: Smart Drill, Resume, Ask Joshua). This is the primary nav for the product.\\r\\n- **Messaging / Inbox** — real messaging feature, not cosmetic. Lives in `src/components/inbox/` (`FloatingMessenger`, `ConversationView`, `ThreadList`) plus `src/hooks/useInbox.ts`. One ongoing 1:1 thread per student with the admin (Joshua). Supports PDF attachments. Gated by `has_chat_access`.\\r\\n- **Practice surfaces** — Drill and Wrong Answer Journal (WAJ) are real product surfaces, not launchers. Core logic in `src/lib/`: `adaptiveEngine`, `drillIntelligence`, `achievementEngine`, `gamification`, `questionLoader`, `streakSystem`, `wajService`.\\r\\n- **Admin** — `AdminDashboard` + `admin-manage-users` edge function. Must be desktop AND mobile responsive. Needs granular per-feature toggle control.\\r\\n- **UI primitives** — shadcn/ui (Radix + `class-variance-authority`) in `src/components/ui/`. Icons from `lucide-react` and `@tabler/icons-react`. Framer Motion for animation. Spline for 3D.\\r\\n- **Styling** — Tailwind 3.4 over HSL custom properties in `src/index.css`, surfaced as tokens in `tailwind.config.ts`. `DESIGN.md` is the visual authority; `.impeccable/design.json` is its machine-readable sidecar. Prefer tokens over ad-hoc hex values, and never add a token name whose CSS variable is not defined - three such names (`accent-bronze`, `accent-warm`, `glow-bronze`) shipped broken for five months and silently removed the focus ring from every shared Button.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Conventions\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Git workflow:** Always commit and push directly to `main`. Never create feature branches or pull requests unless explicitly asked. After completing any code change: stage relevant files, commit with a descriptive message, and push to `main`.\\r\\n- **Push via `.claude/safe-push.sh`, not raw `git push`.** Lovable auto-commits to `main` mid-session; a raw push can get rejected or race a concurrent commit. The script fetches, merges origin/main if it diverged (never rebases, never force-pushes), then pushes.\\r\\n- **Never roll `main` back.** Do not use Lovable\'s \\"Revert to commit\\", \\"revert and resend\\", or history restore, and never reset or force-push `main`. On 2026-09-27 an accidental \\"revert and resend\\" (b998596) silently undid three merged PRs across 121 question-bank files, and students saw the wrong questions again. To undo your own work, `git revert <your SHA>` only. If a Lovable dialog offers a revert, dismiss it; if one fires, stop and tell Joshua before repairing anything.\\r\\n- Path alias `@/` → `./src/` (set in `vite.config.ts` and `tsconfig.json`).\\r\\n- TypeScript strict mode is **off** (`strictNullChecks: false`, `noImplicitAny: false`, `noUnusedLocals: false`). Do not flip these without explicit approval — it would cascade into a very large diff.\\r\\n- Lovable-specific plumbing that must not be removed:\\r\\n  - `lovable-tagger` Vite plugin injects `data-lov-id` in dev\\r\\n  - `vite-plugin-pwa` configured with start URL `/foyer`\\r\\n  - Lovable preview Service Worker guard in `src/main.tsx`\\r\\n- Identity rules: email sign-in, profile identity uses **name** (not username), instructor is displayed as **\\"Joshua\\"**, students display their real profile names.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Cross-tool instruction hygiene\\r\\n\\r\\n`CLAUDE.md` is the fuller project source of truth. `AGENTS.md` is the Codex-facing adapter and should stay aligned without becoming a second full copy.\\r\\n\\r\\n- When updating project instructions, update both files as needed: put durable detail here, and keep `AGENTS.md` as a concise adapter.\\r\\n- When creating a Claude skill that Codex should use, also copy it to `.agents/skills/` with its `SKILL.md` and supporting files.\\r\\n- When creating a Claude agent that Codex should spawn, also create a matching `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` and place the converted instructions in `developer_instructions`.\\r\\n- When adding shared knowledge, put it in `docs/`, `references/`, or `templates/` so every tool can read the same source.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verification (must not skip)\\r\\n\\r\\nAny change to `src/components/` or `src/pages/` is not \\"done\\" until it has been viewed running in the app (dev server + browser tool, e.g. Playwright or chrome devtools MCP), with a screenshot or DOM check as evidence. Do not report a UI change complete on the strength of the diff alone. This has been the single biggest recurring failure across past sessions (repeated \\"it\'s not working\\" / \\"i dont see it\\" corrections) — treat it as a hard gate, not a suggestion.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Responsive fixes carry a wider gate: verify across the full emulate matrix BEFORE pushing, not after Joshua reports it.** That means narrow, mid, and wide viewports plus the sidecar-docked case, every time. A responsive defect that gets pushed as \\"fixed\\" and does not hold costs a second full session — this has already happened (a pushed Home-page fix that did not survive, then 13 screenshots and 8 emulate cycles to actually close it). One matrix pass before the push is cheaper than either.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Product rules (must not regress)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Foyer (`FoyerSidebar` + `FoyerHeroRing`) is the primary navigation. The Foyer additionally hosts a `GooeyDock` quick-launch row well below the orbital ring; this dock is allowed only on `/foyer`. Do not add docks elsewhere.\\r\\n- Inbox is real messaging with back-and-forth threads and PDF attachments, scoped 1:1 per student with admin.\\r\\n- Admin is fully responsive on desktop and mobile.\\r\\n- Do not expose actions users cannot actually perform — no fake analytics, no dead buttons, no misleading placeholders. Prefer truthful fallbacks over fake data.\\r\\n- Onboarding asks for name, not username. Sign-in uses email.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Known gaps (do not invent answers)\\r\\n\\r\\n- Vitest specs exist (80 `src/**/*.test.ts(x)` files as of 2026-07-16); run them with `npm run test`. Playwright is wired with one e2e spec (`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`), run via `npm run test:e2e`.\\r\\n- No Prettier config and no CI workflows. Nothing runs `typecheck`, `lint`, or the tests automatically — `.claude/safe-push.sh` is the only gate, and only for typecheck.\\r\\n- `README.md` is a stub.\\r\\n- `.claude/settings.json` is set up with a permission allowlist for safe dev work (npm scripts, git reads, MCP GitHub reads) and a denylist for destructive ops. No custom `.claude/agents/`. A `SessionStart` auto-pull hook is wired in `.claude/settings.local.json` (runs `.claude/auto-pull-hook.sh`); Codex mirrors it in `.codex/hooks.json`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Skill / agent / command vault\\r\\n\\r\\nThe full skill/agent/command vault lives in the brain root at `~/ai-os/skills/`, `~/ai-os/agents/`, `~/ai-os/commands/` (split into `claude/` and `codex/` subtrees, indexed by `~/ai-os/skills/INDEX.md`). It is inert storage — nothing here auto-loads. To use a vault skill in this project, symlink it into `.claude/skills/` (Codex: `.agents/skills/`). When you create a new skill/agent/command, save it to BOTH this project\'s `.claude/<kind>/` and the vault, so the vault stays the complete catalog.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Agent skills\\r\\n\\r\\n### Issue tracker\\r\\n\\r\\nGitHub Issues on `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db`, via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Triage labels\\r\\n\\r\\nThe five canonical roles, unchanged: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Domain docs\\r\\n\\r\\nMulti-context: `CONTEXT-MAP.md` points at eight per-context glossaries; ADRs are all at the root. It lived in the component\'s memory, she left the\\r\\n * finishing screen, and the answers were gone -- while the recording, which may\\r\\n * have uploaded perfectly, could then be marked by nothing, ever.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport interface StashedRow {\\r\\n  key: string;\\r\\n  runId: string;\\r\\n  assignmentId: string;\\r\\n  studentId: string;\\r\\n  /** `item_order`, which is what makes the key unique within a run. */\\r\\n  itemOrder: number;\\r\\n  /** When it was stashed, which is what bounds it. */\\r\\n  stashedAt: number;\\r\\n  /** The row as `buildRow` made it, ready to be re-sent unchanged. */\\r\\n  row: unknown;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * Keep the rows a run could not save.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * Deliberately its own store rather than a field on the run record, because\\r\\n * the two have different lifetimes and the obvious shared one is wrong. A run\\r\\n * whose recording uploads is discarded the moment it lands -- that is the\\r\\n * point of `discard` -- and the missing-row case is very often exactly that\\r\\n * run: the audio is safely away and the answers are not. Hung off the run\\r\\n * record, the rows would be deleted by the success of the upload.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * So `discard` does not touch them and `purgeStaleRows` bounds them by their\\r\\n * own age instead, on the same seven days.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport async function stashRows(rows: Omit<StashedRow, \\"key\\" | \\"stashedAt\\">[], now = Date.now()): Promise<void> {\\r\\n  if (!available() || !rows.length) return;\\r\\n  try {\\r\\n    const instance = await db();\\r\\n    const tx = instance.transaction(ROWS, \\"readwrite\\");\\r\\n    await Promise.all([\\r\\n      ...rows.map((r) =>\\r\\n        tx.objectStore(ROWS).put({\\r\\n          ...r,\\r\\n          key: `${r.runId}:${String(r.itemOrder).padStart(4, \\"0\\")}`,\\r\\n          stashedAt: now,\\r\\n        } satisfies StashedRow),\\r\\n      ),\\r\\n      tx.done,\\r\\n    ]);\\r\\n  } catch (e) {\\r\\n    // She has finished twenty unbroken minutes. A stash that cannot be written\\r\\n    // leaves the run exactly as ungradable as it already was, and no worse.\\r\\n    console.error(\\"[rrc] could not keep a local copy of the unsaved answers\\", e);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Every row still waiting to be sent, across every run. */\\r\\nexport async function listStashedRows(): Promise<StashedRow[]> {\\r\\n  if (!available()) return [];\\r\\n  try {\\r\\n    return (await (await db()).getAll(ROWS)) as StashedRow[];\\r\\n  } catch {\\r\\n    return [];\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Forget one row: it is safely stored. */\\r\\nexport async function discardRow(key: string): Promise<void> {\\r\\n  if (!available()) return;\\r\\n  try {\\r\\n    await (await db()).delete(ROWS, key);\\r\\n  } catch (e) {\\r\\n    console.error(\\"[rrc] could not clear a recovered answer\\", e);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/**\\r\\n * Drop stashed rows nobody is coming back for.\\r\\n *\\r\\n * The rows outlive their run record by design, so `purgeStale` above cannot\\r\\n * bound them and this does it on the same seven days. It waits for\\r\\n     * an answer, and if the answer is no it holds here rather than spending\\r\\n     * twenty-five unrepeatable minutes on a run nothing can mark.\\r\\n     */\\r\\n    if (!recording && !micRefused) return;\\r\\n    if (micRefused) return;\\r\\n    if (countdown <= 0) {\\r\\n      startedAt.current = runNow();\\r\\n      phaseStartedAt.current = startedAt.current;\\r\\n      stimulusStartedAt.current = startedAt.current;\\r\\n      setCountdown(null);\\r\\n      return;\\r\\n    }\\r\\n    const t = setTimeout(() => setCountdown((n) => (n === null ? null : n - 1)), 1000);\\r\\n    return () => clearTimeout(t);\\r\\n  }, [countdown, runNow, recording, micRefused]);\\r\\n\\r\\n  /*\\r\\n   * `countdown` is a dependency on purpose. This effect returns early during\\r\\n   * the beat, so the ticker can only start when the beat ends -- and the beat\\r\\n   * ending is a change to `countdown`. Without it the effect ran once, at\\r\\n   * mount, and the clock read 0:00 for the whole of every run.\\r\\n   */\\r\\n  useEffect(() => {\\r\\n    if (done || countdown !== null || paused) return;\\r\\n    const tick = setInterval(() => setElapsed(seconds(startedAt.current)), 1000);\\r\\n    return () => clearInterval(tick);\\r\\n  }, [countdown, done, paused, seconds]);\\r\\n\\r\\n  /*\\r\\n   * Hold the app still for the length of the run.\\r\\n   *\\r\\n   * Two things in the browser will end a section without asking. Three groups in the current bank are dropped by\\r\\n * this rule.\\r\\n */\\r\\nexport function buildRcSections(passages: RcIndexPassageWithPt[]): RcSection[] {\\r\\n  const groups = new Map<string, RcIndexPassageWithPt[]>();\\r\\n  for (const p of passages) {\\r\\n    const key = `${p.preptest}:${p.section}`;\\r\\n    const list = groups.get(key);\\r\\n    if (list) list.push(p);\\r\\n    else groups.set(key, [p]);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n\\r\\n  const sections: RcSection[] = [];\\r\\n  for (const group of groups.values()) {\\r\\n    if (group.length !== RC_SECTION_PASSAGE_COUNT) continue;\\r\\n    if (group.some((p) => p.questionCount <= 0)) continue;\\r\\n\\r\\n    const ordered = [...group].sort((a, b) => a.setNumber - b.setNumber);\\r\\n    const questionCount = ordered.reduce((n, p) => n + p.questionCount, 0);\\r\\n\\r\\n    sections.push({\\r\\n      preptest: ordered[0].preptest,\\r\\n      section: ordered[0].section,\\r\\n      passageIds: ordered.map((p) => p.passageId),\\r\\n      passageCount: ordered.length,\\r\\n      questionCount,\\r\\n      fullLength: questionCount >= RC_FULL_SECTION_MIN_QUESTIONS,\\r\\n    });\\r\\n  }\\r\\n\\r\\n  return sections.sort((a, b) => a.preptest - b.preptest || a.section - b.section);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function rcSectionsForPreptest(sections: RcSection[], preptest: number): RcSection[] {\\r\\n  return sections.filter((s) => s.preptest === preptest);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function rcSectionPreptests(sections: RcSection[]): number[] {\\r\\n  return [...new Set(sections.map((s) => s.preptest))].sort((a, b) => a - b);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function rcSectionPace(id: RcSectionPaceId) {\\r\\n  return RC_SECTION_PACES.find((p) => p.id === id) ?? that affect public health or the environment, “risk communication” means persuading the public that the potential risks of such technologies are small and should be ignored. Those who communicate risks in this way seem to believe that lay people do not understand the actual nature of technological risk, and they can cite studies asserting that, although people apparently ignore mundane hazards that pose significant danger, they get upset about exotic hazards that pose little chance of death or injury. Because some risk communicators take this persuasive stance, many lay people see “risk communication” as a euphemism for brainwashing done by experts.\\\\n\\\\nSince, however, the goal of risk communication should be to enable people to make informed decisions about technological risks, a clear understanding about how the public perceives risk is needed. Lay people’s definitions of “risk” are more likely to reflect subjective ethical concerns than are experts’ definitions. Lay people, for example, tend to perceive a small risk to children as more significant than a larger risk to consenting adults who benefit from the risk-creating technology. However, if asked to rank hazards by the number of annual fatalities, without reference to ethical judgments, lay people provide quite reasonable estimates, demonstrating that they have substantial knowledge about many risks. Although some studies claim to demonstrate that lay people have inappropriate concerns about exotic hazards, these studies often use questionable methods, such as asking lay people to rank risks that are hard to compare. In contrast, a recent study showed that when lay people were given the necessary facts and time, they understood the specific risks of electromagnetic fields produced by high-voltage power transmission well enough to make informed decisions.\\\\n\\\\nRisk communication should therefore be based on the principle that people process new information in the context of their existing beliefs. If people know nothing about a topic, they will find messages about that topic incomprehensible. If they have erroneous beliefs, they are likely to misconstrue the messages. Thus, communicators need to know the nature and extent of recipients’ knowledge and beliefs in order to design messages that will not be dismissed or misinterpreted. This need was demonstrated in a research project concerning the public’s level of knowledge about risks posed by the presence of radon in the home. Researchers used open-ended interviews and questionnaires to determine what information should be included in their brochure on radon. This pins them\\r\\n * together, so that day fails here instead of in front of a student.\\r\\n */\\r\\nimport { execFileSync } from \'node:child_process\';\\r\\nimport { readFileSync, readdirSync, mkdtempSync } from \'node:fs\';\\r\\nimport { tmpdir } from \'node:os\';\\r\\nimport { resolve, join } from \'node:path\';\\r\\nimport { describe, it, expect } from \'vitest\';\\r\\nimport { buildPracticeTests } from \'./practiceTest\';\\r\\nimport { buildRcSections, type RcIndexPassageWithPt } from \'@/features/rc/lib/rcSections\';\\r\\nimport type { QuestionManifest } from \'./questionLoader\';\\r\\n\\r\\nconst ROOT = process.cwd();\\r\\nconst DATA = resolve(ROOT, \'public/data\');\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction realRcSections() {\\r\\n  const index = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(DATA, \'rc/rc-index.json\'), \'utf8\'));\\r\\n  const passages: RcIndexPassageWithPt[] = index.preptests.flatMap(\\r\\n    (pt: { preptest: number; passages: Record<string, unknown>[] }) =>\\r\\n      pt.passages.map((p) => ({ ...p, preptest: pt.preptest })),\\r\\n  ) as RcIndexPassageWithPt[];\\r\\n  return buildRcSections(passages);\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nfunction realManifest(): QuestionManifest {\\r\\n  const sections = readdirSync(DATA)\\r\\n    .map((file) => /^PT(\\\\d+)-S(\\\\d+)-LR\\\\.json$/.exec(file))\\r\\n    .filter((m): m is RegExpExecArray => !!m)\\r\\n    .map((m) => ({\\r\\n      pt: Number(m[1]),\\r\\n      section: Number(m[2]),\\r\\n      count: (JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(DATA, m[0]), \'utf8\')) as { status?: string }[])\\r\\n        .filter((q) => q.status !== \'removed\').length,\\r\\n      filename: m[0],\\r\\n    }));\\r\\n  return { sections } as QuestionManifest;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Runs the audit and reads back its machine-readable half. */\\r\\nfunction runAudit() {\\r\\n  const out = join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), \'pt-audit-\')), \'work.json\');\\r\\n  // The script exits 1 while any offered test is short, which is its whole\\r\\n  // point; text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/scripts/knowledge/build-timed-manifest.ts\n@@\n   ensure(blueprints.length > 0, 'No eligible PrepTests');\n   sources.sort((a, b) => a.path.localeCompare(b.path));\n+  for (const source of sources) ensure(hash(readFileSync(resolve(root, source.path))) === source.sha256,\n+    `Canonical source changed during generation: ${source.path}`);\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/docs/implementation-plans/2026-09-30-timed-content-manifest-readiness.md\n+# Exact timed content is prepared for privileged installation\n+\n+Date: 2026-09-30\n+\n+Status: **Generator, deterministic catalog, INSERT-only seed and isolated source-validation tests are prepared. No backend deployment or frontend adoption.** This closes the arbitrary-client-blueprint design gap in the prepared PrepTest writer; it does not establish live atomic enforcement. Ticket #167 remains open.\n+\n+Run from the application checkout:\n+\n+```powershell\n+npx vite-node --script scripts/knowledge/build-timed-manifest.ts\n+npx vite-node --script scripts/knowledge/build-timed-manifest.ts --check\n+npx vitest run src/lib/timedContentManifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1\n+```\n+\n+The generator reads editable `public/data/PT<n>-S<s>-LR.json`, `public/data/rc/rc-index.json`, and each index-referenced `public/data/rc/RC-PT<n>.json`. `scripts/build-question-bank.mjs` identifies individual LR files as editable authority; `_bank.generated.json` is intentionally excluded. RC index membership is checked against its full passage/question files, rather than trusting a count alone.\n+\n+It imports the actual `buildPracticeTests`, `buildRcSections`, and `normalizeQType` runtime rules. LR question order follows the loader's ascending question number; removed positions never enter the queue. PT118 therefore has scored LR S1 (25 questions, excluding Q5), RC S2 (27), and LR S4 (25), with S3 excluded. RC questions retain their native integer IDs, ordered by passage position then question position. Current output contains **59 PrepTests, 177 legs, and 222 hashed source files**.\n+\n+## The writer freezes these server-owned rows\n+\n+The agreed SQL table is `public.timed_content_manifests_v1(manifest_sha256 text, pt integer, blueprint jsonb)`, primary key `(manifest_sha256, pt)`. The transactional writer owns its schema and grants. The generator's SQL artifact creates no schema, policy, role, or grants. It inserts reviewed versions and rejects existing conflicting content instead of replacing it.\n+\n+Each `blueprint` has:\n+\n+| Field | Meaning |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| `pt`, `questionCount`, `rcFullLength` | Runtime PrepTest identity, exact total and full-length RC flag |\n+| `breakAfterLeg`, `breakSeconds` | Fixed existing break rule: after leg 2, 600 seconds |\n+| `legs[]` | Runtime scored sections in published order |\n+| Leg `kind`, `section`, `questionCount`, `qids[]` | Exact ordered leg identity and frozen question queue |\n+| LR `questions[]` | `qid`, `qnum`, normalized `qtype`, `level`, `contentSha256` |\n+| RC `passageIds[]`, `questions[]` | Native integer passage IDs and native question IDs; `qid` is `String(questionId)`, plus `passageId`, `qnum`, `contentSha256` |\n+| RC `passages[]` | `passageId`, `section`, `setNumber`, `contentSha256` |\n+\n+Creation accepts a PrepTest identity and uses the server-configured active manifest hash. A caller cannot choose an arbitrary manifest version, queue, passage set, or leg blueprint. The writer copies the complete blueprint and version into protected parent state, and validates each child command against the frozen matching leg. Manifest rows and historical versions must remain immutable and unavailable to ordinary caller INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Activation is a privileged deployment decision, not a client flag.\n+\n+The generated JSON artifact includes schema version, the blueprint catalog, sorted source-relative paths with SHA-256 hashes, and `manifestSha256`. This hash is SHA-256 of the recursively key-sorted JSON body **excluding the hash field itself**. Arrays retain semantic order. It covers canonical files, relevant runtime rule files and the generator source. It is a whole catalog/version identity, not the digest of PostgreSQL's differently formatted `blueprint::text`. Question fingerprints cover raw source text and choices; file/rule hashes additionally identify answer-key and loader-normalization changes.\n+\n+Artifacts contain no stimuli, prompts, passage text, explanations, choice text, or correct answers. They provide membership/content identity, not a new secure-grading guarantee. Existing client-derived correctness remains the explicit scoring boundary in the timed implementation plan.\n+\n+## Invalid or changing source content prevents generation\n+\n+Validation rejects duplicate or contradictory LR source positions; wrong PT/section identity; unsupported difficulty; missing prompts, choices or keys; duplicate RC passage/question identity; missing choices; index/file roster disagreement; duplicate passage positions in an offered RC leg; and queue/count mismatch. All source hashes are checked again before returning a catalog, so a concurrent canonical edit cannot silently create a mixed snapshot.\n+\n+Tests compare all offered blueprints with the actual runtime builders, pin PT118 removed numbering, verify exact RC ownership and ordered question IDs, reproduce both artifacts byte for byte, and reject injected source identity/duplicate/choice/index defects in isolated temporary fixtures. Changed question content must change its fingerprint and manifest version. These checks do not claim official completeness beyond the bank we ship; the existing practice-test audit remains the authority for gaps in captured official material.\n+\n+Install only after independent review and isolated transactional writer tests. Retain prior manifest rows for historical protected sittings. Fresh live backend metadata, managed deployment route confirmation, and immediate approval for any potentially paid Lovable action are still required before deployment.\n*** End Patch"));

Ticket #167 remains open.\\r\\n\\r\\nRun from the application checkout:\\r\\n\\r\\n```powershell\\r\\nnpx vite-node --script scripts/knowledge/build-timed-manifest.ts\\r\\nnpx vite-node --script scripts/knowledge/build-timed-manifest.ts --check\\r\\nnpx vitest run src/lib/timedContentManifest.test.ts --maxWorkers=1\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThe generator reads editable `public/data/PT<n>-S<s>-LR.json`, `public/data/rc/rc-index.json`, and each index-referenced `public/data/rc/RC-PT<n>.json`. `scripts/build-question-bank.mjs` identifies individual LR files as editable authority; `_bank.generated.json` is intentionally excluded. RC index membership is checked against its full passage/question files, rather than trusting a count alone.\\r\\n\\r\\nIt imports the actual `buildPracticeTests`, `buildRcSections`, and `normalizeQType` runtime rules. LR question order follows the loader\'s ascending question number; removed positions never enter the queue. PT118 therefore has scored LR S1 (25 questions, excluding Q5), RC S2 (27), and LR S4 (25), with S3 excluded. RC questions retain their native integer IDs, ordered by passage position then question position. Current output contains **59 PrepTests, 177 legs, and 222 hashed source files**.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The writer freezes these server-owned rows\\r\\n\\r\\nThe agreed SQL table is `public.timed_content_manifests_v1(manifest_sha256 text, pt integer, blueprint jsonb)`, primary key `(manifest_sha256, pt)`. The transactional writer owns its schema and grants. The generator\'s SQL artifact creates no schema, policy, role, or grants. It inserts reviewed versions and rejects existing conflicting content instead of replacing it.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach `blueprint` has:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Field | Meaning |\\r\\n| --- | --- |\\r\\n| `pt`, `questionCount`, `rcFullLength` | Runtime PrepTest identity, exact total and full-length RC flag |\\r\\n| `breakAfterLeg`, `breakSeconds` | Fixed existing break rule: after leg 2, 600 seconds |\\r\\n| `legs[]` | Runtime scored sections in published order |\\r\\n| Leg `kind`, `section`, `questionCount`, `qids[]` | Exact ordered leg identity and frozen question queue |\\r\\n| LR `questions[]` | `qid`, `qnum`, normalized `qtype`, `level`, `contentSha256` |\\r\\n| RC `passageIds[]`, `questions[]` | Native integer passage IDs and native question IDs; `qid` is `String(questionId)`, plus `passageId`, `qnum`, `contentSha256` |\\r\\n| RC `passages[]` | `passageId`, `section`, `setNumber`, `contentSha256` |\\r\\n\\r\\nCreation accepts a PrepTest identity and uses the server-configured active manifest hash. A caller cannot choose an arbitrary manifest version, queue, passage set, or leg blueprint. The writer copies the complete blueprint and version into protected parent state, and validates each child command against the frozen matching leg. Manifest rows and historical versions must remain immutable and unavailable to ordinary caller INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. Activation is a privileged deployment decision, not a client flag.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe generated JSON artifact includes schema version, the blueprint catalog, sorted source-relative paths with SHA-256 hashes, and `manifestSha256`. This hash is SHA-256 of the recursively key-sorted JSON body **excluding the hash field itself**. Arrays retain semantic order. It covers canonical files, relevant runtime rule files and the generator source. It is a whole catalog/version identity, not the digest of PostgreSQL\'s differently formatted `blueprint::text`. Question fingerprints cover raw source text and choices; file/rule hashes additionally identify answer-key and loader-normalization changes.\\r\\n\\r\\nArtifacts contain no stimuli, prompts, passage text, explanations, choice text, or correct answers. They provide membership/content identity, not a new secure-grading guarantee. Existing client-derived correctness remains the explicit scoring boundary in the timed implementation plan.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Invalid or changing source content prevents generation\\r\\n\\r\\nValidation rejects duplicate or contradictory LR source positions; wrong PT/section identity; unsupported difficulty; missing prompts, choices or keys; duplicate RC passage/question identity; missing choices; index/file roster disagreement; duplicate passage positions in an offered RC leg; and queue/count mismatch. All source hashes are checked again before returning a catalog, so a concurrent canonical edit cannot silently create a mixed snapshot.\\r\\n\\r\\nTests compare all offered blueprints with the actual runtime builders, pin PT118 removed numbering, verify exact RC ownership and ordered question IDs, reproduce both artifacts byte for byte, and reject injected source identity/duplicate/choice/index defects in isolated temporary fixtures. Changed question content must change its fingerprint and manifest version. These checks do not claim official completeness beyond the bank we ship; the existing practice-test audit remains the authority for gaps in captured official material.\\r\\n\\r\\nInstall only after independent review and isolated transactional writer tests. Retain prior manifest rows for historical protected sittings. Fresh live backend metadata, managed deployment route confirmation, and immediate approval for any potentially paid Lovable action are still required before deployment.\\r\\n"}'}]

*/\\r\\nimport type {\\r\\n  RcDrillConfig,\\r\\n  RcLetter,\\r\\n  RcPassage,\\r\\n  RcQuestion,\\r\\n  RcRevealMode,\\r\\n} from \'./rcTypes\';\\r\\n\\r\\n/** One question, flattened out of its already written to rc_attempts in this session. */\\r\\n  recorded: Set<number>;\\r\\n  /** Passages switched into review state (per_passage mode). */\\r\\n  reviewedPassages: Set<number>;\\r\\n  paused: boolean;\\r\\n  submitted: boolean;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function buildItems(passages: RcPassage[]): RcSessionItem[] {\\r\\n  const items: RcSessionItem[] = [];\\r\\n  let number = 1;\\r\\n  passages.forEach((passage, passageIndex) => {\\r\\n    for (const question of passage.questions) {\\r\\n      items.push({ question, passage, number: number++, passageIndex });\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  });\\r\\n  return items;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport function initialState(passages: RcPassage[]): RcSessionState {\\r\\n  return {\\r\\n    items: buildItems(passages),\\r\\n    currentIndex: 0,\\r\\n    answers: new Map(),\\r\\n    eliminations: new Map(),\\r\\n    flagged: new Set(),\\r\\n    revealed: new Set(),\\r\\n    recorded: new Set(),\\r\\n    reviewedPassages: new Set(),\\r\\n [...seen.values()];\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\nexport const isAnswered = (s: RcSessionState, questionId: number) => s.answers.has(questionId);\\r\\n\\r\\n/** True once every question of the passage carries a Live: teaching voice `wiki/teaching-voice.md` (route ALL student-facing copy through it), the business `wiki/entities/aspiring-attorneys.md`, a student\'s record `students/<name>/` (see `students/README.md`), teaching knowledge `corpus/index.md`, and the `wiki/{tasks,hot,dashboard,index,log}.md` hubs named below. Archived read-only reference (pre-rebuild product knowledge, may be stale): `archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/` — product context `…/synthesis/intro-to-lr-product.md`, design system `…/synthesis/intro-to-lr-design.md`, quality bar `…/synthesis/bootcamp-quality-bar.md`, domain index `…/index.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n- `pickup` — start of session. Read `wiki/tasks.md` (the Now / Next / Done ledger) first, then `wiki/hot.md`, `wiki/dashboard.md`, skim `wiki/index.md`, read the latest `wiki/log.md` entry. Emit a 6-8 line briefing (where we left off, Now, Next, open threads, hot, suggested next) and wait. Do not deep-read other pages until pointed at a task.\\r\\n- `wrapup` — end of session. Propose which `## Now` tasks finished and confirm before writing; a wrong \\"Done\\" is the failure to avoid. Then strike finished items through in `wiki/tasks.md` with a date, refresh `wiki/hot.md`, append a dated `wiki/log.md` entry (newest first, distinct label for same-day sessions), update the task anchor.\\r\\n\\r\\n`wiki/tasks.md` is the single source of truth for what is open vs done. Finished work is struck through so a new session never re-runs it. `raw/` in the vault is immutable.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Codex Adapter Layout\\r\\n\\r\\n- `.codex/config.toml`: minimal shared Codex project config. Keep secrets and machine-specific overrides out of this file.\\r\\n- `.codex/agents/`: Codex agent definitions converted from `.claude/agents/*.md` when Claude agents exist. Use `.toml` files with converted instructions in `developer_instructions`.\\r\\n- `.agents/skills/`: repository-local Codex skills copied from `.claude/skills/` when Claude skills exist and Codex should use them. Keep each `SKILL.md` with its supporting files.\\r\\n- `.codex/hooks.json`: existing repository hooks. Playwright is wired with one e2e spec (`e2e/smoke.spec.ts`), run via `npm run test:e2e`.\\r\\n- No Prettier config and no CI workflows.\\r\\n- `README.md` is still minimal.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Agent skills\\r\\n\\r\\n### Issue tracker\\r\\n\\r\\nGitHub Issues on `vnjkoxpl-42905/lsatu-684d89db`, via the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Triage labels\\r\\n\\r\\nThe five canonical roles, unchanged: `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, `wontfix`. text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: C:/Users/Joshu/dev/lsatu-connected-experience/docs/implementation-plans/2026-09-30-timed-child-adapters-readiness.md\n+# Timed LR and RC adapters are prepared without activating existing runners\n+\n+Date: 2026-09-30\n+\n+The new `timedLrAdapter.ts` and `timedRcAdapter.ts` consume the inactive v1 transactional transport. Existing Drill, RC player, legacy session stores and section-history writers do not import them. This is integration preparation, not live enforcement or deployment evidence. #167 remains open.\n+\n+LR composes `TimedPracticeTestStore`. It restores the exact attributed `PracticeSession` queue, position, first answers, flags, switch count and regulation answer IDs. Before creating a checkpoint or close command it verifies canonical source identity and SHA-256 fingerprints against the immutable parent manifest. It imports the existing pure `normalizeQuestionTextFields` function, now exported with no behavior change. Shared passages, prompt repair and prose normalization therefore use the actual QuestionBank rules. Optional loaded QuestionBank rows must agree with the resulting normalized fields and ordered queue. Canonical input must include the entire source section, including removed positions needed by the normalizer; excluded positions cannot enter the scored queue.\n+\n+LR checkpoint commands carry typed selected letters, correctness, milliseconds, flags, switch counts, current position and optional regulation IDs. Close commands require the entire ordered matching answer-key set and an analysis object. Prepared commands are durable before transport; retries retain command ID, revision, epoch and the exact payload. Analysis and client-derived correctness retain the scoring trust boundary documented in the foundation plan. The catalog does not provide a new server-secret answer key.\n+\n+RC composes `TimedWorkClient`. It restores the exact native question/passage attribution, session ownership and saved first-attempt UUIDs. It verifies passage and question text/choice fingerprints against the immutable RC manifest before exposing loaded content or preparing a command. It converts server child rows into the existing RC session and state shapes, deriving end-of-set reveal and section timing from protected parent state. It requires an explicit device identity; foreign writers, pending recovery and expired leases expose paused state. Preparation also checks the current monotonic sample age, preventing a once-valid view from creating commands after lease expiry. Running display time is capped at the account lease. A paused acknowledged child can close through the v1 command.\n+\n+Neither adapter calls a legacy child or parent writer. Capability absence, permission denial, storage failure, malformed source, duplicate attribution or a lost receipt fail closed. A receipt whose parent has advanced to another leg returns no fabricated previous-child view. A future report integration must read the historical acknowledged child or official parent result separately; these adapters never infer a report from an unacknowledged local answer set.\n+\n+Focused tests cover real loader normalization without mutating source input, exact ordered content and SHA identity, owner/source/position/attempt mismatches, regulation attribution, full closeout keys, paused and expired clocks, foreign writers, storage failure, retained command and RC attempt UUIDs after lost replies and reload. Before activation, wire existing runners to these prepared adapters, preserve review-only paths, independently test historical reporting and overtaken receipt recovery, deploy through the confirmed managed route, and verify real multi-device and revoked-access cases. No production writes or Lovable credit actions were performed to prepare them.\n*** End Patch"));

Safe to call from anywhere. */\\r\\nexport function loadRcIndex(): Promise<RcIndex> {\\r\\n  if (!indexPromise) {\\r\\n    indexPromise = fetchJson<RcIndex>(\'/data/rc/rc-index.json\').catch((err) => {\\r\\n      indexPromise = null; // let a later call retry rather than caching a failure\\r\\n      throw err;\\r\\n    });\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  return indexPromise;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Loads (and caches) the flat question search index used by `/rc/search`. */\\r\\nexport function loadRcQuestionIndex(): Promise<RcQuestionIndex> {\\r\\n  if (!questionIndexPromise) {\\r\\n    questionIndexPromise = fetchJson<RcQuestionIndex>(\'/data/rc/rc-question-index.json\').catch(\\r\\n      (err) => {\\r\\n        questionIndexPromise = null; // let a later call retry rather than caching a failure\\r\\n        throw err;\\r\\n      },\\r\\n    );\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  return questionIndexPromise;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Loads (and caches) one PrepTest\'s passages and questions. */\\r\\nexport function loadPreptest(preptest: number): Promise<RcPreptestFile> {\\r\\n  const cached = preptestCache.get(preptest);\\r\\n  if (cached) return cached;\\r\\n\\r\\n  const promise = fetchJson<RcPreptestFile>(`/data/rc/RC-PT${preptest}.json`).catch((err) => {\\r\\n    preptestCache.delete(preptest);\\r\\n    throw err;\\r\\n  });\\r\\n  preptestCache.set(preptest, promise);\\r\\n  return promise;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Finds which PrepTest a passage belongs to, then loads that passage in full. */\\r\\nexport async function loadPassage(passageId: number): Promise<RcPassage | null> {\\r\\n  const index = await loadRcIndex();\\r\\n  const pt = index.preptests.find((t) => t.passages.some((p) => p.passageId === passageId));\\r\\n  if (!pt) return null;\\r\\n  const file = await loadPreptest(pt.preptest);\\r\\n  return file.passages.find((p) => p.passageId === passageId) ?? null;\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Loads several passages, one PrepTest fetch per distinct test, order preserved. */\\r\\nexport async function loadPassages(passageIds: number[]): Promise<RcPassage[]> {\\r\\n  const index = await loadRcIndex();\\r\\n  const ptByPassage = new Map<number, number>();\\r\\n  for (const pt of index.preptests) {\\r\\n    for (const p of pt.passages) ptByPassage.set(p.passageId, pt.preptest);\\r\\n  }\\r\\n  const needed = [...new Set(passageIds.map((id) => ptByPassage.get(id)).filter(Boolean))];\\r\\n  const files = await Promise.all(needed.map((n) => loadPreptest(n as number)));\\r\\n  const byId = new Map<number, RcPassage>();\\r\\n  for (const f of files) for (const p of f.passages) byId.set(p.passageId, p);\\r\\n  return passageIds.map((id) => byId.get(id)).filter(Boolean) as RcPassage[];\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n/** Every passage in the index, flattened, with its PrepTest attached. */\\r\\nexport async function loadAllIndexPassages(): Promise<(RcIndexPassage & { preptest: number })[]> {\\r\\n  const index = await loadRcIndex();\\r\\n  return index.preptests.flatMap((pt) => pt.passages.map((p) => ({ ...p, preptest: pt.preptest })));\\r\\n}\\r\\n\\r\\n"}'}]

A paused acknowledged child can close through the v1 command.\n+\n+RC revisits update the current choice under its stable first-attempt UUID; immutable command receipts preserve acknowledged revisions. Close analysis retains visit/answer-trail and personal marker telemetry in the account session configuration. Both child routes reuse the existing official question/passage panes, retain flags, eliminations, navigation, text size, find, highlights and pause/finish controls, and suppress answer/explanation reveal until the PrepTest returns to its completed report. Rich runner telemetry and optional analysis must be supplied by the final adapters where applicable; these drafts do not switch the existing report/review flows.\r\n\r\n## Receipts and reads support honest recovery\r\n\r\nRPCs:\r\n\r\n- `timed_practice_test_capability_v1()` returns `{contractVersion:1,workKind:\'practice-test\',enabled,operations}`.\r\n- `create_timed_practice_test_v1(p_command jsonb)` accepts operation `create`.\r\n- `commit_timed_work_v1(p_command jsonb)` accepts `claim`, `start-leg`, `checkpoint`, `heartbeat`, `pause`, `resume`, `close-leg`, `start-break`, `finish-break`, and `abandon`.\r\n- `read_timed_practice_test_v1(p_work_id text)` returns an owner-only protected parent, current checkpoint, and server time under a parent share lock. It permits history reads when activation or entitlement is off.\r\n\r\nCommand envelope: `{workKind,workId,commandId,deviceId,expectedRevision,writerEpoch,operation,payload}`. Creation uses revision/epoch zero and payload `{pt,pace,sectionSeconds}`. Control operations take `{}`. An identical retry acknowledges the original operation before current access/revision/lease rejection, while returning the latest parent and checkpoint. Changed payload rejects with `PT412`, distinct from a new-command `PT409` conflict. A replay never reapplies progress or restores an old parent. sectionNumber: number;\r\n  questionNumber: number; stimulus?: string; questionStem: string; answerChoices: LRQuestion['answerChoices'];\r\n  correctAnswer: TimedLetter; questionType?: string; questionDifficulty?: number; Question_Difficulty?: number; status?: string;\r\n}\r\nexport interface TimedLrAnswer {\r\n  qid: string; selected: TimedLetter; correct: boolean; timeMs: number; flagged?: boolean; switchCount?: number;\r\n}\r\nexport interface TimedLrView {\r\n  snapshot: TimedPracticeTestSnapshot;\r\n  session: PracticeSession;\r\n  questions: LRQuestion[];\r\n  clock: ReturnType<typeof timedPracticeTestClock>;\r\n  questionStates: TimedLrQuestionState[];\r\n}\r\nexport interface TimedLrQuestionState { qid: string; timeMs: number; flagged: boolean; eliminations: TimedLetter[] }\r\nconst object = (value: unknown): value is TimedObject => Boolean(value) && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value);\r\nconst integer = (value: unknown): value is number => Number.isSafeInteger(value) && Number(value) >= 0;\r\nconst letter = (value: unknown): value is TimedLetter => typeof value === 'string' && /^[A-E]$/.test(value);\r\nfunction invalid(message: string): never { throw new TimedWorkError('contract', message); }\r\nfunction canonical(value: unknown): string {\r\n  if (Array.isArray(value)) return `[${value.map(canonical).join(',')}]`;\r\n  if (object(value)) return `{${Object.keys(value).sort().map(key => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${canonical(value[key])}`).join(',')}}`;\r\n  return JSON.stringify(value);\r\n}\r\nasync function hash(value: unknown): Promise<string> {\r\n  try { return Array.from(new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', new TextEncoder().encode(canonical(value)))))\r\n    .map(byte => byte.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join(''); }\r\n  catch { return invalid('This browser cannot verify the frozen LR content.'); }\r\n}\r\n\r\n/** Prepared v1-only LR adapter. Runs against dist/ after `npm run build`.\r\n *\r\n * Scans for:\r\n *   - the exact SHA-256s from the manifest (fingerprints of the raw files),\r\n *   - a distinctive prose passage from the canonical Markdown,\r\n *   - the JSONL fenceposts (`"schema_version"` + `"record_id":"lsat-lr-`).\r\n *\r\n * Exits non-zero on any hit so CI/build fails.\r\n */\r\nimport { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync, existsSync } from "node:fs";\r\nimport { resolve, dirname, join } from "node:path";\r\nimport { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";\r\n\r\nconst HERE = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));\r\nconst ROOT = resolve(HERE, "..", "..");\r\nconst DIST = resolve(ROOT, "dist");\r\nconst CONTENT = resolve(ROOT, "content", "lsat", "logical-reasoning");\r\nconst MANIFEST_PATH = join(CONTENT, "logical-reasoning-guide.manifest.json");\r\nconst MD_PATH = join(CONTENT, "logical-reasoning-guide.md");\r\n\r\nif (!existsSync(DIST)) {\r\n  console.error("verify-no-canonical-in-build: dist/ not present.");\r\n  console.error("This check runs as a postbuild step and must not be skipped.");\r\n  console.error("Run `npm run build` before invoking this script.");\r\n  process.exit(2);\r\n}\r\nif (!existsSync(MANIFEST_PATH) || !existsSync(MD_PATH)) {\r\n  console.error("verify-no-canonical-in-build: canonical sources missing at", CONTENT);\r\n  process.exit(2);\r\n}\r\n\r\nconst manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync(MANIFEST_PATH, "utf8"));\r\nconst md = readFileSync(MD_PATH, "utf8");\r\n\r\n// A distinctive passage (>= 80 chars) that only appears in the canonical guide.\r\n// Use the first non-heading paragraph of >= 80 chars.\r\nconst distinctive = md\r\n  .split(/\\r?\\n/)\r\n  .find((l) => l.trim().length >= 80 && !l.trim().startsWith("#") && !l.trim().startsWith("```")) ?? md.slice(0, 120);\r\n\r\nconst needles = [\r\n  { label: "canonical MD sha256", value: manifest.canonical_markdown_sha256 },\r\n  { label: "ingestion JSONL sha256", value: manifest.ingestion_jsonl_sha256 },\r\n  { label: "distinctive MD passage", value: distinctive.trim() },\r\n  { label: "JSONL schema_version fencepost", value: \'"schema_version":"1.1"\' },\r\n  { label: "JSONL record_id fencepost", value: \'"record_id":"lsat-lr-\' },\r\n];\r\n\r\nconst files = [];\r\n(function walk(dir) {\r\n  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {\r\n    const full = join(dir, entry);\r\n    const st = statSync(full);\r\n    if (st.isDirectory()) walk(full);\r\n    else if (/\\.(js|mjs|cjs|css|html|json|txt|map)$/.test(entry)) files.push(full);\r\n  }\r\n})(DIST);\r\n\r\nconst hits = [];\r\nfor (const f of files) {\r\n  const buf = readFileSync(f, "utf8");\r\n  for (const n of needles) {\r\n    if (n.value && buf.includes(n.value)) {\r\n      hits.push({ file: f.replace(ROOT + "/", ""), needle: n.label });\r\n    }\r\n  }\r\n}\r\n\r\nif (hits.length > 0) {\r\n  console.error("FAIL: canonical LSAT guide leaked into build output:");\r\n  for (const h of hits) console.error(`  - ${h.file} :: ${h.needle}`);\r\n  process.exit(1);\r\n}\r\n\r\nconsole.log(`OK verify-no-canonical-in-build: scanned ${files.length} dist files; no canonical guide content present.`);\r\n'}]

/auth/* = sign in flow; admin surfaces\r\n// don\'t need student help (Joshua talks to himself there). /drill = the\r\n// question runner, which carries its own Help control in the header strip\r\n// beside Pause — floating it here parked a bubble over the question card.\r\nconst HIDDEN_PREFIXES = [\'/foyer\', \'/drill\', \'/classroom/drill\', \'/auth\', \'/onboarding\', \'/reset-password\', \'/admin\', \'/teacher\', \'/inbox\'];\r\n\r\nexport function FloatingHelpButton() {\r\n  const { user } = useAuth();\r\n  const { is_admin, loading } = useUserPermissions();\r\n  const { pathname } = useLocation();\r\n  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);\r\n  const anySurfaceOpen = useBottomRightSurfaceOpen();\r\n\r\n  // Publish the Help sheet\'s open state so the messenger + Help launchers stay\r\n  // in lockstep — any open bottom-right surface hides every launcher.\r\n  useEffect(() => {\r\n    setHelpSheetOpen(open);\r\n    return () => setHelpSheetOpen(false);\r\n  }, [open]);\r\n\r\n  if (!user || loading || is_admin) return null;\r\n  if (isOfficialTimedChildPath(pathname) || HIDDEN_PREFIXES.some((p) => pathname === p || pathname.startsWith(`${p}/`))) {\r\n    return null;\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  // De-conflicted anchor: the messenger launcher owns bottom-6 right-6; the\r\n  // Help launcher stacks just above it at bottom-24 right-6 so the two never\r\n  // overlap. Hidden entirely whenever any bottom-right surface is open.\r\n  return (\r\n    <>\r\n      {!anySurfaceOpen && (\r\n        <button\r\n          type="button"\r\n          onClick={() => setOpen(true)}\r\n          aria-label="Get help from Joshua"\r\n          title="Get help from Joshua"\r\n          data-help-overlay\r\n          className="fixed bottom-24 right-6 z-40 inline-flex h-11 w-11 items-center justify-center rounded-full bg-zinc-800 border border-zinc-700 shadow-lg text-zinc-100 hover:bg-zinc-700 transition-colors"\r\n        >\r\n          <HelpCircle className="w-5 h-5" />\r\n        </button>\r\n      )}\r\n      {open && (\r\n        <Suspense fallback={null}>\r\n          <HelpSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} />\r\n        </Suspense>\r\n      )}\r\n    </>\r\n  );\r\n}\r\n M src/App.tsx\n M src/components/help/FloatingHelpButton.tsx\n M src/hooks/useAssignedTodoFeed.ts\n M src/hooks/useScopedStudentWork.test.ts\n M src/hooks/useScopedStudentWork.ts\n M src/lib/railCatalog.test.ts\n M src/lib/studentWorkEvidence.test.ts\n M src/lib/studentWorkEvidence.ts\n M src/pages/MyWorkPage.refetch.test.tsx\n M src/pages/MyWorkPage.tsx\n M src/pages/teacher/students/DossierWork.tsx\n?? src/components/help/FloatingHelpButton.test.tsx\n?? src/lib/officialTimedRoute.ts\n'}]

estimated_minutes integer,\r\n  question_count integer,\r\n  difficulty_min integer,\r\n  difficulty_max integer,\r\n  question_types text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT \'{}\',\r\n  question_features text[] NOT jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT \'{}\'::jsonb,\r\n  source_file text,\r\n  is_published boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,\r\n  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\r\n  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()\r\n);\r\n\r\nALTER TABLE public.guided_drills ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Admins manage guided drills"\r\nON public.guided_drills FOR ALL TO authenticated\r\nUSING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'))\r\nWITH CHECK (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'));\r\n\r\nCREATE INDEX idx_guided_drills_week ON public.guided_drills(week, order_in_week);\r\n\r\nCREATE public.guided_drill_assignments (\r\n  id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\r\n  guided_drill_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES public.guided_drills(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\r\n  student_id uuid NOT NULL,\r\n  class_id text NOT NULL,\r\n  assigned_by uuid NOT NULL,\r\n  assigned_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\r\n  scheduled_for date,\r\n  unlock_at timestamptz,\r\n  status text NOT NULL DEFAULT \'assigned\',\r\n  read_card_at timestamptz,\r\n  started_at timestamptz,\r\n  completed_at timestamptz,\r\n  attempt_session_id uuid,\r\n  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\r\n  updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()\r\n);\r\n\r\nALTER TABLE public.guided_drill_assignments ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Admins manage all assignments"\r\nON public.guided_drill_assignments FOR ALL TO authenticated\r\nUSING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'))\r\nWITH CHECK (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'));\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Students read own assignments"\r\nON public.guided_drill_assignments FOR SELECT TO authenticated\r\nUSING (student_id = auth.uid());\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Students update own assignments"\r\nON public.guided_drill_assignments FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\r\nUSING (student_id = auth.uid())\r\nWITH CHECK (student_id = auth.uid());\r\n\r\nCREATE INDEX idx_gda_student ON public.guided_drill_assignments(student_id, scheduled_for);\r\nCREATE INDEX idx_gda_drill ON public.guided_drill_assignments(guided_drill_id);\r\n\r\nCREATE TRIGGER trg_gda_updated\r\nBEFORE UPDATE ON public.guided_drill_assignments\r\nFOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.update_updated_at_column();\r\n-- Homework Phase A: per-student snapshotted assignments.\r\n-- Rows are created at assign time by admins with question_qids/title/description\r\n-- snapshotted from the parent homework_sets row. Later edits to the set do not\r\n-- mutate already-issued assignments. If the set is deleted, the assignment\r\n-- keeps its snapshot (set_id goes NULL) so the student can still drill it.\r\n\r\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.homework_assignments (\r\n  id                uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\r\n  set_id            uuid REFERENCES public.homework_sets(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,\r\n  student_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\r\n  question_qids     text[] NOT NULL,\r\n  set_title         text NOT NULL,\r\n  set_description   text,\r\n  status            text NOT NULL DEFAULT \'assigned\'\r\n                    CHECK (status IN (\'assigned\', \'in_progress\', \'completed\')),\r\n  started_at        timestamptz,\r\n  completed_at      timestamptz,\r\n  score             numeric CHECK (score IS NULL OR (score >= 0 AND score <= 100)),\r\n  assigned_by       uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id),\r\n  class_id          uuid NOT NULL,\r\n  created_at        timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()\r\n);\r\n\r\nALTER TABLE public.homework_assignments ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\r\n\r\n-- Students: read + update own rows. Immutability of snapshot fields enforced\r\n-- by trigger (guard_homework_assignment_immutables) below.\r\nCREATE POLICY "Students read own assignments"\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments FOR SELECT TO authenticated\r\n  USING (student_id = auth.uid());\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Students update own assignments"\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\r\n  USING (student_id = auth.uid())\r\n  WITH CHECK (student_id = auth.uid());\r\n\r\n-- Admin full CRUD (bypasses the immutability trigger via role check).\r\nCREATE POLICY "Admins read all assignments"\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments FOR SELECT TO authenticated\r\n  USING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'));\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Admins insert assignments"\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments FOR INSERT TO authenticated\r\n  WITH CHECK (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\') AND assigned_by = auth.uid());\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Admins update assignments"\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\r\n  USING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'))\r\n  WITH CHECK (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'));\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Admins delete assignments"\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments FOR DELETE TO authenticated\r\n  USING (public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\'));\r\n\r\n-- Immutability guard: students cannot mutate snapshot or attribution columns.\r\n-- Allowed student writes: status, started_at, completed_at, score.\r\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.guard_homework_assignment_immutables()\r\nRETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$\r\nBEGIN\r\n  IF public.has_role(auth.uid(), \'admin\') THEN\r\n    RETURN NEW;\r\n  END IF;\r\n\r\n  IF NEW.set_id           IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.set_id           OR\r\n     NEW.student_id       IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.student_id       OR\r\n     NEW.question_qids    IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.question_qids    OR\r\n     NEW.set_title        IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.set_title        OR\r\n     NEW.set_description  IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.set_description  OR\r\n     NEW.assigned_by      IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.assigned_by      OR\r\n     NEW.class_id         IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.class_id         OR\r\n     NEW.created_at       IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.created_at THEN\r\n    RAISE EXCEPTION \'homework_assignments: snapshot columns are immutable for non-admin users\';\r\n  END IF;\r\n\r\n  RETURN NEW;\r\nEND;\r\n$$;\r\n\r\nDROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS homework_assignments_guard_immutables ON public.homework_assignments;\r\nCREATE TRIGGER homework_assignments_guard_immutables\r\n  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.homework_assignments\r\n  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.guard_homework_assignment_immutables();\r\n\r\n-- Index for student Classroom queries: scan by student, filter by status.\r\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS homework_assignments_student_status_idx\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments (student_id, status, created_at DESC);\r\n\r\n-- At most one active assignment per (student, set). A completed assignment\r\n-- does not block re-issuing the same set.\r\nCREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS homework_assignments_active_unique\r\n  ON public.homework_assignments (student_id, set_id)\r\n  WHERE status <> \'completed\' AND set_id IS NOT NULL;\r\n-- Per-user key/value store for bootcamp progress autosave.\r\n-- The bootcamp persistence layer stores small JSON records keyed by\r\n-- (table_name, record_id). This mirrors them to the backend so each\r\n-- profile keeps all of their progress across devices/sessions.\r\n\r\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.bootcamp_kv (\r\n  user_id      uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\r\n  table_name   text        NOT NULL,\r\n  record_id    text        NOT NULL,\r\n  data         jsonb       NOT NULL,\r\n  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),\r\n  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, table_name, record_id)\r\n);\r\n\r\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS bootcamp_kv_user_table_idx\r\n  ON public.bootcamp_kv (user_id, table_name);\r\n\r\nGRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON public.bootcamp_kv TO authenticated;\r\nGRANT ALL ON public.bootcamp_kv TO service_role;\r\n\r\nALTER TABLE public.bootcamp_kv ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Users read own bootcamp data"\r\n  ON public.bootcamp_kv FOR SELECT TO authenticated\r\n  USING (auth.uid() = user_id);\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Users insert own bootcamp data"\r\n  ON public.bootcamp_kv FOR INSERT TO authenticated\r\n  WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Users update own bootcamp data"\r\n  ON public.bootcamp_kv FOR UPDATE TO authenticated\r\n  USING (auth.uid() = user_id)\r\n  WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id);\r\n\r\nCREATE POLICY "Users delete own bootcamp data"\r\n  ON public.bootcamp_kv FOR DELETE TO authenticated\r\n  USING (auth.uid() = user_id);\r\n\r\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.bootcamp_kv_touch_updated_at()\r\nRETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\r\nBEGIN\r\n  NEW.updated_at = now();\r\n  RETURN NEW;\r\nEND;\r\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public;\r\n\r\nDROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS bootcamp_kv_touch ON public.bootcamp_kv;\r\nCREATE TRIGGER bootcamp_kv_touch\r\n  BEFORE UPDATE ON public.bootcamp_kv\r\n  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.bootcamp_kv_touch_updated_at();\r\nrg: supabase/migrations/20260507*: The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect. const sql=`-- PROPOSAL ONLY. Never executed during preparation.
-- SQL-role/RLS proof, not an authenticated HTTP/JWT test.
-- Each successful candidate insertion is rolled back inside its subtransaction.
-- The final deliberate exception aborts the outer transaction even if the caller
-- stops before the explicit ROLLBACK. Do not remove the exception/rollback guards.
BEGIN;
SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '3s';
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '30s';
DO $audit$
DECLARE
  teacher constant uuid := '5ff160ef-016e-4ab5-aab1-55c7a2ad888f';
  tester constant uuid := 'd763bfe6-d710-4c4b-90ff-4b3a20929211';
  spec record; candidate jsonb; columns_sql text; values_sql text; statement_sql text;
  pk text; next_attempt integer; positive_valid boolean; positive_error text;
  outcome text; error_class text; state text; message text; report jsonb := '[]';
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'authenticated' OR public.has_role(tester,'admin') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Requires reviewed migration session and a non-admin tester';
  END IF;
  FOR spec IN SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ${vals}
    ) AS sources(table_name,predicate,variant)
  LOOP
    pk := CASE WHEN spec.table_name='bootcamp_kv' THEN 'record_id' ELSE 'id' END;
    -- This read is privileged, and only selects the named existing teacher fixture.
    EXECUTE format('SELECT to_jsonb(t) FROM public.%I t WHERE %s ORDER BY t.%I LIMIT 1',
      spec.table_name,replace(spec.predicate,'teacher',quote_literal(teacher)::text),pk) INTO candidate;
    IF candidate IS NULL THEN
      report := report || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('table',spec.table_name,
        'variant',spec.variant,'foreignFixtureExists',false,'outcome','unverified-no-fixture'));
      CONTINUE;
    END IF;
    candidate := candidate || jsonb_build_object(pk,gen_random_uuid()::text);
    IF spec.table_name='rc_attempts' THEN
      -- Existing first-attempt uniqueness would otherwise mask RLS with 23505.
      candidate := candidate || '{"is_first_attempt":false}'::jsonb;
    ELSIF spec.table_name='activity_item_responses' THEN
      SELECT max(attempt_no)+1 INTO next_attempt FROM public.activity_item_responses
        WHERE assignment_id=(candidate->>'assignment_id')::uuid
          AND student_id=(candidate->>'student_id')::uuid
          AND item_order=(candidate->>'item_order')::integer AND attempt_no<2147483647;
      candidate := candidate || jsonb_build_object('attempt_no',next_attempt);
    ELSIF spec.table_name='attempts' AND spec.variant='mixed-attribution' THEN
      -- Probe the actual asymmetric policy: own class_id but foreign user_id.
      candidate := candidate || jsonb_build_object('class_id',tester::text);
    END IF;
    SELECT string_agg(format('%I',column_name),',' ORDER BY ordinal_position),
      string_agg(format('r.%I',column_name),',' ORDER BY ordinal_position)
      INTO columns_sql,values_sql FROM information_schema.columns
      WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name=spec.table_name
        AND is_generated='NEVER' AND is_identity='NO';
    statement_sql := format('INSERT INTO public.%I (%s) SELECT %s FROM jsonb_populate_record(NULL::public.%I,$1) r',
      spec.table_name,columns_sql,values_sql,spec.table_name);
    positive_valid := false; positive_error := null;
    BEGIN
      PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub',teacher::text,true);
      PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims',jsonb_build_object('sub',teacher,'role','authenticated')::text,true);
      -- Positive schema/trigger control only; this privileged check is NOT RLS proof.
      EXECUTE statement_sql USING candidate;
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'positive candidate rolled back' USING ERRCODE='ZQ001';
    EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
      GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS state=RETURNED_SQLSTATE;
      positive_valid := state='ZQ001';
      IF NOT positive_valid THEN positive_error := state; END IF;
    END;
    IF NOT positive_valid THEN
      report := report || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('table',spec.table_name,
        'variant',spec.variant,'foreignFixtureExists',true,'positiveCandidateValid',false,
        'outcome','unverified-positive-control','errorClass',positive_error));
      CONTINUE;
    END IF;
    outcome := 'unverified'; error_class := null;
    BEGIN
      PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub',tester::text,true);
      PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims',jsonb_build_object('sub',tester,'role','authenticated')::text,true);
      EXECUTE 'SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated';
      IF current_user<>'authenticated' OR auth.uid() IS DISTINCT FROM tester OR public.has_role(auth.uid(),'admin') THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Ordinary actor validation failed' USING ERRCODE='ZQ003';
      END IF;
      EXECUTE statement_sql USING candidate;
      -- Even an unexpectedly permitted INSERT cannot survive this inner rollback.
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'foreign insertion permitted, rolled back' USING ERRCODE='ZQ002';
    EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN
      GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS state=RETURNED_SQLSTATE,message=MESSAGE_TEXT;
      error_class := state;
      outcome := CASE
        WHEN state='ZQ002' THEN 'FAIL-insert-permitted-rolled-back'
        WHEN state='42501' AND message ILIKE '%row-level security%' THEN 'PASS-RLS-denied'
        WHEN state='42501' THEN 'denied-other-permission-or-trigger'
        WHEN state LIKE '23%' THEN 'unverified-constraint'
        ELSE 'unverified-other-error' END;
    END;
    report := report || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('table',spec.table_name,
      'variant',spec.variant,'foreignFixtureExists',true,'positiveCandidateValid',true,
      'outcome',outcome,'errorClass',error_class));
  END LOOP;
  -- Expected failure response carries only source-level results, never records.
  RAISE EXCEPTION 'ROLLBACK_ONLY_INSERT_REPORT %',report USING ERRCODE='ZQ999';
END
$audit$;
ROLLBACK;
`;

Null user_id remains supported for the existing legacy attribution shape. It does not alter, backfill or delete historical attempts, change SELECT behavior, grant privileges or modify the separate dedicated timed-executor policy. The runtime guard requires the exact reviewed named policy and refuses an additional ordinary permissive INSERT policy that could override this condition.\n+\n+Before deployment, independently review and execute the rollback-only candidate probe. Then validate three ordinary-role cases against the proposed rule: own class plus own user succeeds; own class plus null user succeeds; own class plus foreign user is denied explicitly by RLS. Fresh UUIDs avoid uniqueness collisions, and successful candidates must be rolled back. Also rerun protected timed LR closeout under its dedicated executor and ordinary protected-write exclusion. is_identity='NO';\n+  statement_sql := format('INSERT INTO public.attempts (%s) SELECT %s FROM jsonb_populate_record(NULL::public.attempts,$1) r',columns_sql,values_sql);\n+  FOREACH variant IN ARRAY ARRAY['own-owner','own-null'] LOOP\n+    candidate := original || jsonb_build_object('id',gen_random_uuid()::text,\n+      'class_id',tester::text,'user_id',CASE WHEN variant='own-owner' THEN to_jsonb(tester::text) ELSE 'null'::jsonb END);\n+    BEGIN\n+      PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub',tester::text,true);\n+      PERFORM set_config('request.jwt.claims',jsonb_build_object('sub',tester,'role','authenticated')::text,true);\n+      EXECUTE 'SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated';\n+      IF current_user<>'authenticated' OR auth.uid() IS DISTINCT FROM tester\n+        OR public.has_role(auth.uid(),'admin') THEN\n+        RAISE EXCEPTION 'Ordinary actor validation failed' USING ERRCODE='ZQ003';\n+      END IF;\n+      EXECUTE statement_sql USING candidate;\n+      GET DIAGNOSTICS inserted=ROW_COUNT;\n+      IF inserted<>1 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Expected one exact candidate' USING ERRCODE='ZQ004'; END IF;\n+      -- GET STACKED DIAGNOSTICS state=RETURNED_SQLSTATE;\n+      report := report || jsonb_build_array(jsonb_build_object('table','attempts',\n+        'variant',variant,'foreignFixtureExists',true,\n+        'outcome',CASE WHEN state='ZQ001' THEN 'PASS-insert-permitted-rolled-back' ELSE 'FAIL-or-unverified' END,\n+        'errorClass',state));\n+    END;\n+  END LOOP;\n+  -- Abort the outer transaction
